title: Vance & Kinder x Ghostbird Content Interview

summary.short_summary: Marisol shared the story of winning Meridian Air Systems away from a nine-year incumbent supplier after two missed ship dates, tying the win back to Vance & Kinder's reputation for reliable lead times. Revenue is up roughly 40% year over year with three new hires this quarter. sentences.text: Hey Marisol, good to see you! How was Chicago?
Oh my gosh, it was a lot. Good, but a lot. The show floor was bigger than last year, way more foot traffic.
Nice, did the new booth setup help?
It did. We had people stop just because the fastener wall display looked different than everybody else's boring folding table.
Love that. Okay, well let's dive in, I've got a handful of questions for you today, should take us like ten, fifteen minutes. First, anything big happen this month business-wise?
Actually yeah, huge one. We landed Meridian Air Systems. They're an HVAC manufacturer out of Ohio, decent size, and they were with our biggest competitor for like nine years.
Whoa, nine years. How'd that happen?

Their old supplier missed two ship dates in a row on a rush order and it cost them a production line shutdown. Their procurement guy called us because he'd met one of our reps at a trade show like a year ago and just remembered we talked a lot about lead times.
That's such a good story. So it wasn't even a sales pitch that won it, it was just being memorable a year earlier.
Exactly. And honestly that's kind of been our whole thing since I took over. We can't always win on price, steel's steel, but we can win on your stuff shows up when we say it will.
Okay I'm already writing a post title in my head. Let's keep going though, how's revenue looking this year overall?
We're up about forty percent year over year. Which is wild because I keep waiting for it to slow down and it just hasn't.
Any hiring because of that?
Yeah, three new people this quarter. Two in the warehouse, one inside sales rep, kid named Colton, twenty-four years old, first real sales job.
Okay hold that thought, I want to come back to Colton in a second. First, I want to hear the put your dad on the phone story again because I think I only got half of it last time.

Okay so, when I took over from my dad six years ago, we had this one customer, Big Sky Fabrication, been with us since like 1994. And the owner, older guy, calls in, doesn't know I've taken over yet, and I answer and he goes hi honey, is Gary around?
Oh no.
And I said, this is Marisol, I run the company now, how can I help? And he just goes quiet for a second and then says well, can you put your dad on the phone.
What did you do?

I didn't get mad, which honestly surprised me. I just said, he retired, but I've been running ops here for three years already, so I promise I know your account better than he does at this point. What do you need? And I just helped him with his order like normal.
Two weeks later he calls back, orders are fine, and at the end of the call he goes, you know, you actually know what you're talking about. Which, low bar, but I'll take it.
Is he still a customer?
Still a customer. Actually one of our top twenty accounts now. He introduced us to two other fab shops in Montana.
Okay that's the post. That's a whole post right there. Let's talk about Colton for a second, what happened with him?

So he's brand new, still learning the product line, and he closed his first deal on his own last week. Small account, like four thousand dollars, but he called me practically shaking he was so excited.
That's awesome, do you remember what you told him?
I told him I still remember my first sale after I took over, and it was smaller than his. Everybody starts small. I think sometimes owners forget to say that out loud to new people.

Good, that's a second post, maybe a shorter one about mentoring the next generation of the sales team. Okay, switching gears a little, anything going on outside of work you want to talk about? I remember you mentioned training for something.
Oh, the half marathon. Yeah, I'm doing it with our ops manager, Dave, actually. We started running together at like six a.m. before work because neither of us can find time otherwise.
How's training going?
Painful. But good. We've actually ended up talking through half our Q4 planning on those runs, which was not the point originally.
That's a great detail actually, like the best planning happens at six a.m. on a run, not in a conference room.
Basically, yeah.
Okay let's hold that one until after the race though, so we can use an actual finish line photo instead of a stock training photo. When is it?
Three weeks from Saturday.
Perfect, I'll follow up with you the Monday after for a picture. Okay, last thing, anything from the ERP or systems side worth mentioning, or are we good on content for now?
We're mid-rollout on a new inventory system, but it's not exciting yet, ask me again next month, it'll either be a disaster story or a win story by then.
Deal. Okay I've got plenty here, the Meridian win, the put your dad on the phone story, and the Colton mentoring moment. I'll get drafts of all three to you by end of week.
Sounds good. Oh, one more thing, can you grab that photo from my phone, the one of the booth setup in Chicago? I'll text it to you.
Yes please, that'll be great for whichever post ends up needing a visual. Alright, thanks Marisol, talk soon.
Thanks Jarrich, bye!
